clue.text: Excited smoker's accessory — or office accessory?

parts.note: excited or elated can be described as high
a lighter is what a smoker uses to light up

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether an item belongs to a jittery smoker's kit or sits on an office desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A highlighter is a fluorescent marker pen, a standard piece of office stationery.

clue.text: Partner beginning to hate the Beach Boys?

indicators.note: the beginning of the word hate is its first letter

parts.note: the Beach Boys were an American band: a US band

explanation.surface: Someone's other half has started to loathe the Californian surf-pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband is a marriage partner, a spouse.

clue.text: It's lacking in seriousness producing extra money

indicators.note: being lacking in something means it is missing, so the letters are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: gravity is seriousness or solemnity
read as 'it is': IT is what is missing, the 'is' being part of the link

explanation.surface: Something frivolous turns out to be lucrative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's lacking in' reads 'IT is lacking in': remove IT from GRAVITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravy is informal slang for unearned extra money or an easy bonus.

clue.text: Stir leaderless crew and employee on TV

indicators.note: without a leader means the first letter is dropped from the word for prison

parts.note: stir and clink are both slang for prison
to crew a vessel is to man it

explanation.surface: An instruction to rouse a ship's company that has lost its captain, plus a broadcasting worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is not a verb here but the slang noun for jail, CLINK, which loses its leader C.
explanation.definitionFit: A link man is the presenter who connects the items of a television or radio programme.

clue.text: Wave, say, as diplomatic move

definitions.meaning: a wave of the hand is an example of a bodily signal
an action made to show goodwill

explanation.surface: A friendly wave serving as a piece of statecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave is a hand movement that signals something, and a token action of goodwill between parties is also called one.

clue.text: Drains set to deteriorate, giving problem in schedule?

indicators.note: letters that deteriorate break down and fall out of their order

explanation.surface: Plumbing left to decay causes delays to a timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness is the trouble that knocks a timetable out of kilter.

clue.text: Boxer amid break not one prone to fantasy?

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the boxer's name sits within the word for a break

parts.note: a rest is a break from activity
Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer

explanation.surface: A fighter in a pause between rounds, who is no daydreamer.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist deals with things as they actually are rather than with fancies.

clue.text: Bats fluttering in wet conditions first off stay dry

indicators.note: bats fluttering move about erratically, so the letters are rearranged
the first letter is taken off

parts.note: rain gives wet conditions

explanation.surface: Bats flit about in the drizzle while someone tries to keep dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay dry' is not about the weather: to stay dry is to avoid alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain, especially from drinking alcohol, which is what staying dry means.

clue.text: A boar and a pig running wild around house? It's a recognised fear

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for house
animals running wild scatter in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Two farm animals loose around a dwelling sounds frightening, and the fear has a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running wild' rearranges A BOAR A PIG into AGORAPBIA, placed 'around' HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Agoraphobia is a clinically recognised phobia of open or crowded spaces.

clue.text: Ruler losing time with speaker's opening gibes

indicators.note: losing means the letter for time is dropped from the ruler's title

parts.note: a tsar was the ruler of Russia

indicators.note: as a speaker says it, so the letters follow the word as heard

parts.note: a chasm is a deep opening or gap

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch's speaking slot begins with insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker's' signals the sound of CHASM, written CASM.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is mocking, cutting remarks, so taunts and jibes collectively.

clue.text: Film about a new hospital with poor distrust of others?

indicators.note: the word for film goes about the following letters

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass
ropy is British slang for poor in quality

explanation.surface: A movie about a fledgling medical centre in a bad way, all about suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: MIST goes about A and N. ROPY is everyday British slang for shoddy or unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Misanthropy is dislike and mistrust of humankind in general.

clue.text: Literary heroine book cast in vital female part

indicators.note: to cast something is to throw it off, so the book's letter is discarded

parts.note: Emma Bovary, heroine of Flaubert's Madame Bovary

explanation.surface: A story's leading lady given an important female role in a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks theatrical but means thrown off.
explanation.definitionFit: The ovary is the essential female reproductive organ that produces eggs.

clue.text: A rum suit I fancy in holiday destination

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a strange outfit on a sunny trip abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauritius is an Indian Ocean island nation popular with tourists for beach holidays.

clue.text: Heating device with club

parts.note: and can mean with, together with
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A heater accompanied by a golf club or cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron, or firedog, is a metal support holding logs in an open fireplace.

clue.text: In list, artist replaces European medic

indicators.note: replaces means one letter is swapped out for the artist's letters

parts.note: a register is an official list
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: On a roster, a painter takes the place of a continental doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The second E of REGISTER becomes RA.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK hospitals a registrar is a doctor in the grade below consultant.

clue.text: Team not at any time heading south?

parts.note: ever means at any time

indicators.note: heading south means going downward, the word turned the wrong way round

explanation.surface: A side that never manages to go anywhere but down the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading south' reverses 'not' even in an across light; the surface hints at relegation, but the team is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League football club from Liverpool.

clue.text: They're paid in tribute to get on in Syrian city

indicators.note: in means the word for growing older is placed inside the city's name

parts.note: Homs is a city in western Syria
to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: Honours are offered to growing old in a city in Syria.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is respect shown publicly, and one 'pays homage' in honouring someone.

clue.text: Gets together announcement of increased cost of beef?

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the words are taken by how they are said

parts.note: if beef costs more, the price of meat is up: meat's up

explanation.surface: A notice that steak has gone up in price.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet up is to come together with someone by arrangement.

clue.text: Claims benefit having two partners in old Asian city bar area

indicators.note: in places the two partners inside the trimmed city name
bar means except, so the letter for area is removed

parts.note: Saigon is the former name of Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A man with two partners in a Saigon bar applies for state handouts.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, to sign on is to register as unemployed and claim welfare payments.

clue.text: Spiteful saying backed with ridicule

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the word for saying is reversed

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb
pish is an exclamation of contempt or derision

explanation.surface: A malicious remark supported by mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means sharply irritable and stinging in manner, like a wasp.

clue.text: Course pursued by hawks?

parts.note: hawks are not birds but warmongers, and the route they follow is the path to battle

explanation.surface: The flight line followed by birds of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the warpath means set on hostility, the stance of aggressive political hawks.

clue.text: Moving past this entrance could be trespassing?

indicators.note: moving letters shift them into a new order, here the answer's with those of past

explanation.surface: Going beyond this doorway might count as unlawful entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters plus those of PAST, all moved about, make TRESPASSING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the formal word for the act or means of going in.

clue.text: A big blow in retirement cutting drink, source of sweetness?

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into the drink, placed in its middle

parts.note: beer is a drink

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: a gust is a big blow of wind: a gust

explanation.surface: A heavy punch in old age interrupts a drinker's pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retirement' turns A GUST backwards, and 'cutting' slices that into the drink after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Beet sugar is sucrose extracted from sugar beet, a source of sweetening.

clue.text: Trouble in the past besets old King

indicators.note: besets means surrounds, so the past word goes around the king

parts.note: ago means in the past
GR, Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: Long ago, hardship surrounded an elderly monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive behaviour or hassle.

clue.text: Bring together cycling in tea-growing area

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from one end to the other

parts.note: Assam, the state in north-east India famous for its tea

explanation.surface: Riding a bike around the plantations of India.
explanation.walkthrough: The final AM of ASSAM cycles to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate.

clue.text: Judge largely found round centre of courts provides confidence

indicators.note: found round means located encircling, so the judging word surrounds the middle letters
largely means mostly, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to assess is to judge or evaluate

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A magistrate, mostly located around the law courts, reassures people.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure someone is to promise them, inspiring certainty.

clue.text: Surprised reaction after poster is put in outstanding scholarly institution

indicators.note: after means this exclamation goes at the end
is put in places the poster word inside the word for outstanding

parts.note: ace means excellent, outstanding
an ad, advertisement, can be a poster
my! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An exclamation after a notice goes up in an excellent college.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or society devoted to learning.

clue.text: Mother, perhaps, almost completed dissertation in interlude

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a mother is an example of a parent
a thesis is a dissertation submitted for a degree

explanation.surface: A mum nearly finishing her PhD write-up takes a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A parenthesis is a digression or pause in speech, so an interval or aside.
